headline: Orders surge to a record while profit cools
summary_short: Baker Hughes posted Q2 revenue of $6,742M, down 2.4% y/y as divested units weighed on the top line, while net income fell to $681M (-2.9% y/y, -26.8% q/q) after a one-time Q1 disposition gain rolled off; cash rose to $15,727M on debt issued for the Chart acquisition.
summary_long: Revenue of $6,742M fell 2.4% y/y (up 2.4% q/q) on the PSI/SPC dispositions. GAAP diluted EPS of $0.68 dropped 4.2% y/y, 26.9% q/q; net income of $681M fell 2.9% y/y, 26.8% q/q, mainly as a one-time Q1 disposition gain didn't repeat. Adjusted net income and Adjusted EBITDA ($1,231M) still rose both q/q and y/y on volume, price, productivity and cost-out gains, partly offset by inflation. Orders hit a record $10.5B and RPO $40.1B on IET strength; the company raised full-year IET order guidance and its 2026-2028 IET orders outlook to over $45B. Cash rose to $15,727M after $9.9B of debt issued to fund the Chart acquisition; shareholders' equity grew to $19,908M.

drivers.explanation: Orders hit a record $10.5B (IET $7.1B) and RPO a record $40.1B on Gas Technology strength; the company raised full-year IET order guidance and its multi-year IET orders outlook to over $45B, and closed the Chart Industries acquisition in July.
Y/y revenue decline was 'driven by the impact of the PSI and SPC dispositions'; the 2% sequential increase is not explained in the release.

GAAP net income fell 26.8% q/q mainly because a one-time ~$721M gain on business dispositions recognized in Q1 did not recur; adjusted net income, which excludes that gain, rose 12% sequentially per the company's own reconciliation table.

The company's own Adjusted EBITDA ($1,231M, distinct from this summary's shard-sourced 'EBITDA' KPI) rose both q/q and y/y, per management 'primarily driven by higher volume, price, productivity, FX, and cost-out initiatives', partly offset by inflation.
